headline: Every major is still under its 200-day line, but momentum and whale flow are arguing with the fear gauge
paragraphs: Start with the regime, because it's unanimous: BTC, ETH, SOL, XRP, BNB, DOGE and ADA are all trading below their 200-day averages, none carry a golden cross, and the distances from 12-month highs run from BTC's relatively tame -46.6% to ADA's brutal -82.0%. This is not a market where one laggard is dragging down a healthy pack. Every asset in the board is still working through a drawdown of some size, and that context matters for everything that follows.

Layer momentum on top and you get a genuine divergence worth naming. BTC's RSI sits at 62.1 and ETH's at 65.3, both with MACD above signal, which is the kind of reading you'd normally associate with an asset pushing into new highs, not one still 47-60% off its peak. XRP and ADA show the same MACD-bullish, RSI-mid-50s pattern. SOL is the outlier among majors with RSI 56.1 but MACD below signal, momentum cooling rather than building. So the tape is showing short-term strength layered on top of a longer-term downtrend, a bounce inside a drawdown, not a trend reversal by itself.

Positioning adds texture rather than confirmation. BTC funding is barely positive (0.0023% per 8h, 2.5% annualized), longs paying a token amount to hold $2.05B of open interest with a long/short ratio of 1.55, and yet in the last 18 hours longs ate $19.6M of liquidations versus $6.9M for shorts, despite price rising 2.26%. That's a crowded long side getting flushed even as it's proven directionally right today, which says the leverage was tight going in. ETH funding is negative (-1.1% annualized, shorts paying longs) but shorts still took the bigger liquidation hit, $10.0M versus $5.2M for longs, an inversion worth flagging rather than explaining away. Down the cap stack, SOL, XRP and DOGE all show negative funding paired with long/short ratios stacked heavily toward longs (2.85 to 3.64), and longs dominate their liquidations too. Read plainly: crowds are long, some of them are getting paid a small amount to be long, and it's the long side taking the pain when volatility hits. That's a fragile setup, not a confident one.

Flow data cuts two ways. On 27 Jul, spot BTC ETFs saw -$11.6M net, and the five-session total is -$204.5M with 3 of those days moving the same direction, a real if modest outflow stretch, though the $51.4B cumulative total is still firmly positive. ETH ETFs did the opposite on the same day, +$11.7M, and +$77.5M over five sessions, but with only 1 same-direction day that's a thinner, less persistent signal. Stablecoin float sits at $306.4B, down 1.35% over 30 days, so the dry powder sitting on the sidelines has been shrinking slightly rather than building. Whale wallets, meanwhile, show a net $2.78M moving off exchanges in the last 24 hours, with two-way traffic in the hundreds of millions (BTC $139.8M onto Coinbase Institutional against $146.3M off it, similar churn at Okex and Kraken). The weekly net figures bounce between +$1.34B, -$0.32B, -$0.13B and +$0.90B, no clean trend, just volatility around a mild net outflow bias.

Set all of that against a Fear & Greed reading of 29, sitting near the top of its own 30-day range of 11 to 33. Sentiment is still labeled Fear even as BTC is up 2.26% on the day, MACD is bullish across most majors, and whale flow is net leaving exchanges. That gap between how the crowd says it feels and what the derivatives and flow data show is the notable tension today, not any single number in isolation.

What to watch from here: whether BTC's five-session ETF flow flips back positive and whether same_direction_days starts stacking in one direction, whether funding on BTC or ETH moves further from flat (a sign leverage is building conviction one way), and whether any major actually reclaims its 200-day average, which none currently hold. Those are the specific conditions that would tell you the picture in this data has actually changed.
